To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) use case based requirements engineering is a promising method for eliciting, documenting and validating functional requirements; (2) use case models can serve as a basis for test cases and for reliability assessment; (3) the combination of multiple perspectives in inspections may not give a higher defect detection rate, but may be more time consuming; and (4) the transition of use case models into high-level design can be supported by use case based architectural design.

use cases can be used for: - requirements elicitation, specification and validation - system test case generation and assessment of reliability - documenting the distribution of functional requirements on architectural elements - prioritising requirements in a release-driven development process
Use cases are a suitable vehicle for eliciting, structuring and documenting functional requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of use cases for requirements engineering, and how use cases can support system testing and design.
the role of use cases in software development, in particular how to integrate use case modelling with other software engineering activities.
the role of use cases and requirements validation, and the transition from requirements to design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of use cases in requirements engineering is beneficial and that the results of the studies presented in this thesis provide a good basis for the further use of use cases.
the use of use cases and scenarios is an important vehicle for eliciting, analysing, specifying and validating system requirements.
the application of use cases in the requirements engineering process can be beneficial for the development of high-quality software systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use case modelling is a promising vehicle for eliciting, documenting, analysing, specifying and validating functional requirements, which may also be a basis for system verification and validation.
use cases are a promising vehicle for requirements engineering, but that the process of requirements elicitation and specification is more complex than what is often described.
use cases are a promising vehicle in requirements engineering, but the use of use cases should be integrated in an overall requirements engineering approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that

use cases can be applied for eliciting, analysing, specifying, and validating requirements and that use cases can also be applied for documenting how requirements are distributed on system components and for supporting system testing and reliability analysis.
use cases can be used for elicitation, specification, validation and design, but that their application should be tailored to the context of use.
use cases can be successfully applied to support requirements engineering activities, such as elicitation, analysis, design, validation and prioritisation.
